claim: The change leaves these as they are: - It adds no interruption of work already running on a worker thread. A cancelled call's database query keeps running on its SQL worker thread until it finishes or the engine's statement timeout stops it. Nothing but the query's own end stops it when `statement_timeout_ms = 0`, or when it is a MySQL statement other than `SELECT`, which MySQL's `MAX_EXECUTION_TIME` does not cover. Server shutdown waits for such threads. - It adds no thread pool of its own. Since #300, Anthropic calls are awaited on the async Anthropic client and use no worker thread, so cancelling a call cancels its Anthropic request's await. Database driver work runs on SQL Lens's dedicated SQL worker pool from #300 (`src/sqllens/agent/integrations/sql_threads.py`: eight threads behind an `asyncio.Semaphore`), kept apart from asyncio's default executor; a query that finds every slot busy waits up to 60 s for one, then fails with `SqlWorkersBusyError` without running. The ChromaDB memory store keeps its own two-thread pool. - It leaves the synchronous memory-store calls of `import_memory` and the memory-administration MCP tools on the event loop, so those tools still block it while they run. - It leaves the scratch CSV write after each query, `df.to_csv`, and the read-only and row-level-security guards' SQL parsing on the event loop. - It adds no progress notifications and no acknowledge-now / fetch-later job API. A `query_database` call still holds its request open until the agent run ends, so a question that takes longer than a client's timeout still times out for that client.
